title: JEE Advanced 2024 · Paper 2
instr: Official JEE (Advanced) 2024 Paper 2 with the final answer key published by the organising IIT (IIT Madras).
51 questions: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, 17 in each subject, in four sections. Total 180 marks.
Section 1 – single correct option: +3 if correct, −1 if wrong, 0 if not answered.
Section 2 – one or more correct options: +4 if you choose all the correct options; +3 / +2 / +1 if you choose only some of the correct options and no wrong one; −2 in all other cases.

questions.text: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of $$\tan\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)-2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\right)\right)$$ is
questions.sol:
Let $a=\sin^{-1}\dfrac35$, so $\tan a=\dfrac34$; let $b=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}$, so $\tan b=\dfrac12$.
$\tan 2b=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac12}{1-\frac14}=\dfrac43$.
$\tan(a-2b)=\dfrac{\frac34-\frac43}{1+\frac34\cdot\frac43}=\dfrac{-\frac{7}{12}}{2}=-\dfrac{7}{24}$ → (B).

questions.text: Let $S=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R} : x\ge 0,\ y\ge 0,\ y^2\le 4x,\ y^2\le 12-2x \text{ and } 3y+\sqrt8\,x\le 5\sqrt8\right\}$. If the area of the region $S$ is $\alpha\sqrt2$, then $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$y^2=4x$ and $y^2=12-2x$ meet at $(2,2\sqrt2)$; the line $3y+2\sqrt2\,x=10\sqrt2$ also passes through $(2,2\sqrt2)$ and meets $y=0$ at $x=5$ (while $y^2=12-2x$ meets it at $x=6$).
So for $0\le y\le 2\sqrt2$ the region runs from the parabola $x=\dfrac{y^2}{4}$ to the line $x=\dfrac{10\sqrt2-3y}{2\sqrt2}=5-\dfrac{3y}{2\sqrt2}$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt2}\left(5-\dfrac{3y}{2\sqrt2}-\dfrac{y^2}{4}\right)dy=10\sqrt2-3\sqrt2-\dfrac{4\sqrt2}{3}=\dfrac{17}{3}\sqrt2$.
$\alpha=\dfrac{17}{3}$ → (B).

questions.text: Let $k\in\mathbb{R}$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0+}\left(\sin(\sin kx)+\cos x+x\right)^{\frac{2}{x}}=e^6$, then the value of $k$ is
questions.sol:
The form is $1^\infty$, so the limit is $e^{L}$ with $L=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0+}\dfrac{2}{x}\left(\sin(\sin kx)+\cos x+x-1\right)$.
$\sin(\sin kx)\approx kx$, $\cos x-1\approx -\dfrac{x^2}{2}$, so $L=2(k+1)$.
$2(k+1)=6\Rightarrow k=2$ → (B).

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $$f(x)=\begin{cases} x^2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{x^2}\right), & \text{if } x\ne 0,\\ 0, & \text{if } x=0.\end{cases}$$ Then which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: $f(x)=0$ has infinitely many solutions in the interval $\left[\dfrac{1}{10^{10}},\infty\right)$.
$f(x)=0$ has no solutions in the interval $\left[\dfrac{1}{\pi},\infty\right)$.
The set of solutions of $f(x)=0$ in the interval $\left(0,\dfrac{1}{10^{10}}\right)$ is finite.
$f(x)=0$ has more than 25 solutions in the interval $\left(\dfrac{1}{\pi^2},\dfrac{1}{\pi}\right)$.
questions.sol:
For $x\ne0$: $f(x)=0\iff \dfrac{\pi}{x^2}=n\pi\iff x=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt n}$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
(A) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt n}\ge10^{-10}\iff n\le10^{20}$: finitely many → false.
(B) $x=1\ge\dfrac1\pi$ is a solution → false. (C) $n>10^{20}$ gives infinitely many → false.
(D) $\dfrac{1}{\pi^2}<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt n}<\dfrac1\pi\iff \pi^2<n<\pi^4$, i.e. $n=10,11,\ldots,97$: $88$ solutions, more than $25$ → (D).

questions.text: Let $S$ be the set of all $(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$ such that $$\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{\sin(x^2)(\log_e x)^{\alpha}\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)}{x^{\alpha\beta}(\log_e(1+x))^{\beta}}=0.$$ Then which of the following is (are) correct?
questions.sol:
As $x\to\infty$: $\sin\left(\dfrac1{x^2}\right)\sim\dfrac1{x^2}$ and $\log_e(1+x)\sim\log_e x$.
So the expression behaves like $\sin(x^2)\,\dfrac{(\log_e x)^{\alpha-\beta}}{x^{2+\alpha\beta}}$; with $\sin(x^2)$ bounded and oscillating, the limit is $0$ iff $2+\alpha\beta>0$, or $2+\alpha\beta=0$ and $\alpha-\beta<0$.
(A) $2+\alpha\beta=-1<0$ → not in $S$. (B) $2+\alpha\beta=1>0$ → in $S$. (C) $2+\alpha\beta=1>0$ → in $S$.
(D) $2+\alpha\beta=0$ but $\alpha-\beta=3>0$, so $\sin(x^2)(\log_e x)^3$ does not tend to $0$ → not in $S$.
Answer: (B), (C).

questions.text: A straight line drawn from the point $P(1,3,2)$, parallel to the line $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{2}=\dfrac{z-6}{1}$, intersects the plane $L_1 : x-y+3z=6$ at the point $Q$. Another straight line which passes through $Q$ and is perpendicular to the plane $L_1$ intersects the plane $L_2 : 2x-y+z=-4$ at the point $R$. Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: The length of the line segment $PQ$ is $\sqrt6$
The centroid of the triangle $PQR$ is $\left(\dfrac43,\dfrac{14}{3},\dfrac53\right)$
The perimeter of the triangle $PQR$ is $\sqrt2+\sqrt6+\sqrt{11}$
questions.sol:
Line through $P$: $(1+t,\,3+2t,\,2+t)$. In $L_1$: $(1+t)-(3+2t)+3(2+t)=6\Rightarrow 2t=2$, $t=1$, so $Q=(2,5,3)$ and $PQ=\sqrt{1+4+1}=\sqrt6$ → (A) true.
Line through $Q$ along $(1,-1,3)$: $(2+s,\,5-s,\,3+3s)$. In $L_2$: $2(2+s)-(5-s)+(3+3s)=-4\Rightarrow 6s=-6$, $s=-1$, so $R=(1,6,0)$ → (B) false.
Centroid $=\left(\dfrac{1+2+1}{3},\dfrac{3+5+6}{3},\dfrac{2+3+0}{3}\right)=\left(\dfrac43,\dfrac{14}3,\dfrac53\right)$ → (C) true.
$QR=\sqrt{1+1+9}=\sqrt{11}$, $PR=\sqrt{0+9+4}=\sqrt{13}$, so perimeter $=\sqrt6+\sqrt{11}+\sqrt{13}$ → (D) false.
Answer: (A), (C).

questions.text: Let $A_1,B_1,C_1$ be three points in the $xy$-plane. Suppose that the lines $A_1C_1$ and $B_1C_1$ are tangents to the curve $y^2=8x$ at $A_1$ and $B_1$, respectively. If $O=(0,0)$ and $C_1=(-4,0)$, then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: The length of the line segment $OA_1$ is $4\sqrt3$
The length of the line segment $A_1B_1$ is $16$
The orthocenter of the triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ is $(0,0)$
The orthocenter of the triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ is $(1,0)$
questions.sol:
For $y^2=8x$ ($a=2$), the tangent at $(2t^2,4t)$ is $ty=x+2t^2$. Through $(-4,0)$: $2t^2=4$, $t=\pm\sqrt2$.
So $A_1=(4,4\sqrt2)$, $B_1=(4,-4\sqrt2)$. $OA_1=\sqrt{16+32}=4\sqrt3$ → (A) true; $A_1B_1=8\sqrt2\ne16$ → (B) false.
By symmetry the altitude from $C_1$ is the $x$-axis. Slope of $B_1C_1=\dfrac{-4\sqrt2}{8}=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, so the altitude from $A_1$ has slope $\sqrt2$: $y-4\sqrt2=\sqrt2(x-4)$, which meets $y=0$ at $x=0$.
Orthocentre $=(0,0)$ → (C) true, (D) false.
Answer: (A), (C).

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$, and $g:\mathbb{R}\to(0,\infty)$ be a function such that $g(x+y)=g(x)g(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$. If $f\left(\dfrac{-3}{5}\right)=12$ and $g\left(\dfrac{-1}{3}\right)=2$, then the value of $$\left(f\left(\dfrac14\right)+g(-2)-8\right)g(0)$$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Additivity gives $f(r)=r\,f(1)$ for every rational $r$: $f\left(-\dfrac35\right)=-\dfrac35f(1)=12\Rightarrow f(1)=-20$, so $f\left(\dfrac14\right)=-5$.
Similarly $g(r)=g(1)^r$ for rational $r$ and $g(0)=1$: $g(1)^{-1/3}=2\Rightarrow g(1)=\dfrac18$, so $g(-2)=8^2=64$.
Value $=(-5+64-8)\times1=51$.

questions.text: A bag contains $N$ balls out of which $3$ balls are white, $6$ balls are green, and the remaining balls are blue. Assume that the balls are identical otherwise. Three balls are drawn randomly one after the other without replacement. For $i=1,2,3$, let $W_i, G_i$, and $B_i$ denote the events that the ball drawn in the $i^{\text{th}}$ draw is a white ball, green ball, and blue ball, respectively. If the probability $P(W_1\cap G_2\cap B_3)=\dfrac{2}{5N}$ and the conditional probability $P(B_3\mid W_1\cap G_2)=\dfrac29$, then $N$ equals ______.
questions.sol:
$P(B_3\mid W_1\cap G_2)=\dfrac{N-9}{N-2}=\dfrac29\Rightarrow 9N-81=2N-4\Rightarrow N=11$.
Check: $P(W_1\cap G_2\cap B_3)=\dfrac{3}{11}\cdot\dfrac{6}{10}\cdot\dfrac{2}{9}=\dfrac{2}{55}=\dfrac{2}{5N}$ ✓.
$N=11$.

questions.text: Let the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $$f(x)=\dfrac{\sin x}{e^{\pi x}}\,\dfrac{\left(x^{2023}+2024x+2025\right)}{\left(x^2-x+3\right)}+\dfrac{2}{e^{\pi x}}\,\dfrac{\left(x^{2023}+2024x+2025\right)}{\left(x^2-x+3\right)}.$$ Then the number of solutions of $f(x)=0$ in $\mathbb{R}$ is ______.
questions.sol:
$f(x)=\dfrac{(\sin x+2)\left(x^{2023}+2024x+2025\right)}{e^{\pi x}\left(x^2-x+3\right)}$.
$\sin x+2>0$, $e^{\pi x}>0$ and $x^2-x+3>0$ (discriminant $-11$), so $f(x)=0\iff h(x)=x^{2023}+2024x+2025=0$.
$h'(x)=2023x^{2022}+2024>0$, so $h$ is strictly increasing with exactly one real root ($h(-1)=0$).
Number of solutions $=1$.

questions.text: Let $\vec p=2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec q=\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$. If for some real numbers $\alpha,\beta$, and $\gamma$, we have $$15\hat i+10\hat j+6\hat k=\alpha\left(2\vec p+\vec q\right)+\beta\left(\vec p-2\vec q\right)+\gamma\left(\vec p\times\vec q\right),$$ then the value of $\gamma$ is _______.
questions.sol:
$\vec p\times\vec q=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&1&3\\1&-1&1\end{vmatrix}=4\hat i+\hat j-3\hat k$, and $|\vec p\times\vec q|^2=26$.
$\vec p\times\vec q$ is perpendicular to $2\vec p+\vec q$ and $\vec p-2\vec q$, so dotting both sides with it:
$15(4)+10(1)+6(-3)=26\gamma\Rightarrow 52=26\gamma\Rightarrow\gamma=2$.

questions.text: A normal with slope $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}$ is drawn from the point $(0,-\alpha)$ to the parabola $x^2=-4ay$, where $a>0$. Let $L$ be the line passing through $(0,-\alpha)$ and parallel to the directrix of the parabola. Suppose that $L$ intersects the parabola at two points $A$ and $B$. Let $r$ denote the length of the latus rectum and $s$ denote the square of the length of the line segment $AB$. If $r:s=1:16$, then the value of $24a$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$L$ is $y=-\alpha$; it meets $x^2=-4ay$ at $x=\pm2\sqrt{a\alpha}$, so $s=AB^2=16a\alpha$; $r=4a$.
$r:s=4a:16a\alpha=1:16\Rightarrow\alpha=4$.
Point $(2at,-at^2)$: slope of tangent $=-t$, so slope of normal $=\dfrac1t=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}\Rightarrow t=\sqrt6$; normal: $y+6a=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}\left(x-2\sqrt6\,a\right)$.
Through $(0,-4)$: $-4+6a=-2a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac12$.
$24a=12$.

questions.text: Let the function $f:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $$f(t)=\begin{cases}(-1)^{n+1}\,2, & \text{if } t=2n-1,\ n\in\mathbb{N},\\ \dfrac{(2n+1-t)}{2}f(2n-1)+\dfrac{(t-(2n-1))}{2}f(2n+1), & \text{if } 2n-1<t<2n+1,\ n\in\mathbb{N}.\end{cases}$$ Define $g(x)=\displaystyle\int_1^x f(t)\,dt$, $x\in(1,\infty)$. Let $\alpha$ denote the number of solutions of the equation $g(x)=0$ in the interval $(1,8]$ and $\beta=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1+}\dfrac{g(x)}{x-1}$. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to _____.
questions.sol:
$f(1)=2$, $f(3)=-2$, $f(5)=2$, $f(7)=-2$, $f(9)=2$, and $f$ is linear in between: a zigzag through zero at $t=2,4,6,8$.
Each triangle has area $1$, so $g(2)=1$, $g(3)=0$, $g(4)=-1$, $g(5)=0$, $g(6)=1$, $g(7)=0$, $g(8)=-1$, with $g$ monotonic between these points.
Zeros of $g$ in $(1,8]$: $x=3,5,7$, so $\alpha=3$.
$\beta=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1+}\dfrac{g(x)}{x-1}=g'(1^+)=f(1)=2$.
$\alpha+\beta=5$.

questions.text:
Let $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ and $X$ be the set of all relations $R$ from $S$ to $S$ that satisfy both the following properties:
i. $R$ has exactly $6$ elements.
ii. For each $(a,b)\in R$, we have $|a-b|\ge 2$.
Let $Y=\{R\in X : \text{The range of } R \text{ has exactly one element}\}$ and $Z=\{R\in X : R \text{ is a function from } S \text{ to } S\}$.
Let $n(A)$ denote the number of elements in a set $A$.

If $n(X)={}^{m}C_6$, then the value of $m$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Ordered pairs in $S\times S$ with $|a-b|\ge2$: $36-6$ (with $a=b$) $-10$ (with $|a-b|=1$) $=20$.
$X$ consists of all $6$-element subsets of these $20$ pairs, so $n(X)={}^{20}C_6$.
$m=20$.

questions.text:
Let $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ and $X$ be the set of all relations $R$ from $S$ to $S$ that satisfy both the following properties:
i. $R$ has exactly $6$ elements.
ii. For each $(a,b)\in R$, we have $|a-b|\ge 2$.
Let $Y=\{R\in X : \text{The range of } R \text{ has exactly one element}\}$ and $Z=\{R\in X : R \text{ is a function from } S \text{ to } S\}$.
Let $n(A)$ denote the number of elements in a set $A$.

If the value of $n(Y)+n(Z)$ is $k^2$, then $|k|$ is _____________.
questions.sol:
$Y$: all $6$ pairs have the same second entry $b$, so we need at least $6$ values of $a$ with $|a-b|\ge2$; but for $b=1,\ldots,6$ there are only $4,3,3,3,3,4$ such $a$. So $n(Y)=0$.
$Z$: a function assigns each $a$ one image $b$ with $|a-b|\ge2$: $4,3,3,3,3,4$ choices for $a=1,\ldots,6$.
$n(Z)=4\cdot3^4\cdot4=1296$.
$k^2=0+1296\Rightarrow|k|=36$.

questions.text:
Let $f:\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\to[0,1]$ be the function defined by $f(x)=\sin^2 x$ and let $g:\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\to[0,\infty)$ be the function defined by $g(x)=\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi x}{2}-x^2}$.

The value of $$2\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}f(x)g(x)\,dx-\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}g(x)\,dx$$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$g\left(\dfrac\pi2-x\right)=\sqrt{\dfrac\pi2\left(\dfrac\pi2-x\right)-\left(\dfrac\pi2-x\right)^2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi x}{2}-x^2}=g(x)$.
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^2x\,g(x)\,dx$. Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac\pi2-x$: $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^2x\,g(x)\,dx$.
Adding: $2I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}g(x)\,dx$.
So the value is $0$.

questions.text:
Let $f:\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\to[0,1]$ be the function defined by $f(x)=\sin^2 x$ and let $g:\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\to[0,\infty)$ be the function defined by $g(x)=\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi x}{2}-x^2}$.

The value of $$\dfrac{16}{\pi^3}\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}f(x)g(x)\,dx$$ is ____________.
questions.sol:
From the previous question, $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}f g\,dx=\dfrac12\int_0^{\pi/2}g\,dx$.
$y=g(x)$ is the upper half of $\left(x-\dfrac\pi4\right)^2+y^2=\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)^2$, so $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}g\,dx=\dfrac12\pi\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)^2=\dfrac{\pi^3}{32}$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}fg\,dx=\dfrac{\pi^3}{64}$, and $\dfrac{16}{\pi^3}\cdot\dfrac{\pi^3}{64}=\dfrac14=0.25$.

questions.text:
A region in the form of an equilateral triangle (in $x$-$y$ plane) of height $L$ has a uniform magnetic field $\vec B$ pointing in the $+z$-direction. A conducting loop PQR, in the form of an equilateral triangle of the same height $L$, is placed in the $x$-$y$ plane with its vertex P at $x=0$ in the orientation shown in the figure. At $t=0$, the loop starts entering the region of the magnetic field with a uniform velocity $\vec v$ along the $+x$-direction. The plane of the loop and its orientation remain unchanged throughout its motion.
Which of the following graph best depicts the variation of the induced emf ($E$) in the loop as a function of the distance ($x$) starting from $x=0$?
questions.sol:
Measure depth $s$ from $x=0$ into the field triangle; both triangles have width $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\times$(distance from their apex). With P at distance $x$, the loop occupies $x-L\le s\le x$ and the field $0\le s\le L$.
$0\le x\le L$: overlap width is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\min(s,\,x-s)$, area $A=\dfrac{x^2}{2\sqrt3}$, so $|E|=Bv\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{Bvx}{\sqrt3}$: grows linearly to $\dfrac{BvL}{\sqrt3}$ at $x=L$.
$L\le x\le 2L$: $A=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}-2(x-L)^2\right]$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{4L-3x}{\sqrt3}$.
This falls linearly, is zero at $x=\dfrac{4L}{3}$ (between $L$ and $\dfrac{3L}{2}$), and at $x=2L$ equals $-\dfrac{2L}{\sqrt3}$: the emf reverses and reaches twice the earlier peak. At $x=2L$ the overlap vanishes, so $E=0$ beyond.
Linear rise to $L$, reversal crossing zero before $\dfrac{3L}{2}$ and a peak of double size at $2L$ → (A).

questions.text:
A particle of mass $m$ is under the influence of the gravitational field of a body of mass $M\ (\gg m)$. The particle is moving in a circular orbit of radius $r_0$ with time period $T_0$ around the mass $M$. Then, the particle is subjected to an additional central force, corresponding to the potential energy $V_c(r)=m\alpha/r^3$, where $\alpha$ is a positive constant of suitable dimensions and $r$ is the distance from the center of the orbit. If the particle moves in the same circular orbit of radius $r_0$ in the combined gravitational potential due to $M$ and $V_c(r)$, but with a new time period $T_1$, then $(T_1^2-T_0^2)/T_1^2$ is given by
[$G$ is the gravitational constant.]
questions.sol:
Extra force: $F=-\dfrac{dV_c}{dr}=\dfrac{3m\alpha}{r^4}$, directed outward.
Before: $m\omega_0^2r_0=\dfrac{GMm}{r_0^2}$. After: $m\omega_1^2r_0=\dfrac{GMm}{r_0^2}-\dfrac{3m\alpha}{r_0^4}$.
$\dfrac{T_1^2-T_0^2}{T_1^2}=1-\dfrac{\omega_1^2}{\omega_0^2}=\dfrac{3\alpha/r_0^5}{GM/r_0^3}=\dfrac{3\alpha}{GMr_0^2}$ → (A).

questions.text: A metal target with atomic number $Z=46$ is bombarded with a high energy electron beam. The emission of X-rays from the target is analyzed. The ratio $r$ of the wavelengths of the $K_\alpha$-line and the cut-off is found to be $r=2$. If the same electron beam bombards another metal target with $Z=41$, the value of $r$ will be
questions.sol:
The cut-off wavelength $\lambda_c=\dfrac{hc}{eV}$ depends only on the beam, so it is unchanged.
Moseley: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{K\alpha}}\propto(Z-1)^2$, so $r\propto\dfrac{1}{(Z-1)^2}$.
$r'=2\times\left(\dfrac{45}{40}\right)^2=2\times1.2656=2.53$ → (A).

questions.text: A thin stiff insulated metal wire is bent into a circular loop with its two ends extending tangentially from the same point of the loop. The wire loop has mass $m$ and radius $r$ and it is in a uniform vertical magnetic field $B_0$, as shown in the figure. Initially, it hangs vertically downwards, because of acceleration due to gravity $g$, on two conducting supports at P and Q. When a current $I$ is passed through the loop, the loop turns about the line PQ by an angle $\theta$ given by
questions.sol:
Magnetic moment $\mu=I\pi r^2$, along the normal to the loop. When the loop has turned by $\theta$ about PQ, its normal makes angle $90^\circ-\theta$ with the vertical field.
Magnetic torque about PQ: $I\pi r^2B_0\sin(90^\circ-\theta)=I\pi r^2B_0\cos\theta$.
Gravity acts at the centre, a distance $r$ from PQ: torque $mgr\sin\theta$.
Balance: $I\pi r^2B_0\cos\theta=mgr\sin\theta\Rightarrow\tan\theta=\dfrac{\pi rIB_0}{mg}$ → (A).

questions.text:
A small electric dipole $\vec p_0$, having a moment of inertia $I$ about its center, is kept at a distance $r$ from the center of a spherical shell of radius $R$. The surface charge density $\sigma$ is uniformly distributed on the spherical shell. The dipole is initially oriented at a small angle $\theta$ as shown in the figure. While staying at a distance $r$, the dipole is free to rotate about its center.
If released from rest, then which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
[$\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space.]
options: The dipole will undergo small oscillations at any finite value of $r$.
The dipole will undergo small oscillations at any finite value of $r>R$.
The dipole will undergo small oscillations with an angular frequency of $\sqrt{\dfrac{2\sigma p_0}{\epsilon_0 I}}$ at $r=2R$.
The dipole will undergo small oscillations with an angular frequency of $\sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma p_0}{100\epsilon_0 I}}$ at $r=10R$.
questions.sol:
Inside the shell ($r<R$) the field is zero, so there is no torque and no oscillation → (A) false.
Outside, $E=\dfrac{\sigma R^2}{\epsilon_0r^2}$ (radial), and the restoring torque $p_0E\sin\theta\approx p_0E\theta$ gives SHM for any $r>R$ → (B) true.
$\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac{p_0E}{I}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma p_0R^2}{\epsilon_0Ir^2}}$.
$r=2R$: $\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma p_0}{4\epsilon_0I}}$ → (C) false. $r=10R$: $\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma p_0}{100\epsilon_0I}}$ → (D) true.
Answer: (B), (D).

questions.text:
A table tennis ball has radius $(3/2)\times10^{-2}$ m and mass $(22/7)\times10^{-3}$ kg. It is slowly pushed down into a swimming pool to a depth of $d=0.7$ m below the water surface and then released from rest. It emerges from the water surface at speed $v$, without getting wet, and rises up to a height $H$. Which of the following option(s) is(are) correct?
[Given: $\pi=22/7$, $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, density of water $=1\times10^3\ \text{kg m}^{-3}$, viscosity of water $=1\times10^{-3}$ Pa-s.]
options: The work done in pushing the ball to the depth $d$ is $0.077$ J.
If we neglect the viscous force in water, then the speed $v=7$ m/s.
If we neglect the viscous force in water, then the height $H=1.4$ m.
The ratio of the magnitudes of the net force excluding the viscous force to the maximum viscous force in water is $500/9$.
questions.sol:
$V=\dfrac43\cdot\dfrac{22}{7}\cdot(1.5\times10^{-2})^3=1.4143\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^3$; buoyancy $=\rho Vg=0.14143$ N; weight $=0.03143$ N.
Net upward force (excluding viscosity) $F=0.11$ N. Work to push it slowly to $0.7$ m: $0.11\times0.7=0.077$ J → (A) true.
Without viscosity: $a=\dfrac{0.11}{(22/7)\times10^{-3}}=35\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, $v^2=2(35)(0.7)=49$, $v=7$ m/s → (B) true.
$H=\dfrac{v^2}{2g}=2.45$ m → (C) false.
Maximum viscous force (at $v=7$ m/s): $6\pi\eta rv=6\cdot\dfrac{22}{7}\cdot10^{-3}\cdot1.5\times10^{-2}\cdot7=1.98\times10^{-3}$ N; ratio $=\dfrac{0.11}{1.98\times10^{-3}}=\dfrac{500}{9}$ → (D) true.
Answer: (A), (B), (D).

questions.text:
A positive, singly ionized atom of mass number $A_{\text{M}}$ is accelerated from rest by the voltage $192$ V. Thereafter, it enters a rectangular region of width $w$ with magnetic field $\vec B_0=0.1\hat k$ Tesla, as shown in the figure. The ion finally hits a detector at the distance $x$ below its starting trajectory.
[Given: Mass of neutron/proton $=(5/3)\times10^{-27}$ kg, charge of the electron $=1.6\times10^{-19}$ C.]
Which of the following option(s) is(are) correct?
options: The value of $x$ for $H^+$ ion is $4$ cm.
The value of $x$ for an ion with $A_{\text{M}}=144$ is $48$ cm.
For detecting ions with $1\le A_{\text{M}}\le196$, the minimum height $(x_1-x_0)$ of the detector is $55$ cm.
The minimum width $w$ of the region of the magnetic field for detecting ions with $A_{\text{M}}=196$ is $56$ cm.
questions.sol:
Radius $R=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB}$. For $H^+$: $\sqrt{2\cdot\frac53\times10^{-27}\cdot1.6\times10^{-19}\cdot192}=3.2\times10^{-22}$, so $R=\dfrac{3.2\times10^{-22}}{1.6\times10^{-20}}=0.02$ m.
The ion turns through a semicircle and comes back out, so $x=2R=4$ cm → (A) true.
$R\propto\sqrt{A_{\text{M}}}$: for $A_{\text{M}}=144$, $x=12\times4=48$ cm → (B) true.
$x_0=4$ cm ($A_{\text{M}}=1$), $x_1=14\times4=56$ cm ($A_{\text{M}}=196$): height $52$ cm → (C) false.
Minimum width for $A_{\text{M}}=196$ is $R=28$ cm → (D) false.
Answer: (A), (B).

questions.text: The dimensions of a cone are measured using a scale with a least count of $2$ mm. The diameter of the base and the height are both measured to be $20.0$ cm. The maximum percentage error in the determination of the volume is ______.
questions.sol:
$V=\dfrac{\pi D^2h}{12}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=2\dfrac{\Delta D}{D}+\dfrac{\Delta h}{h}$.
With $\Delta D=\Delta h=0.2$ cm: $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=2\left(\dfrac{0.2}{20}\right)+\dfrac{0.2}{20}=0.03$.
Maximum percentage error $=3$.

questions.text: A ball is thrown from the location $(x_0,y_0)=(0,0)$ of a horizontal playground with an initial speed $v_0$ at an angle $\theta_0$ from the $+x$-direction. The ball is to be hit by a stone, which is thrown at the same time from the location $(x_1,y_1)=(L,0)$. The stone is thrown at an angle $(180-\theta_1)$ from the $+x$-direction with a suitable initial speed. For a fixed $v_0$, when $(\theta_0,\theta_1)=(45^\circ,45^\circ)$, the stone hits the ball after time $T_1$, and when $(\theta_0,\theta_1)=(60^\circ,30^\circ)$, it hits the ball after time $T_2$. In such a case, $(T_1/T_2)^2$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Both have the same acceleration $g$, so their relative velocity is constant. To meet, the vertical components must be equal: $u\sin\theta_1=v_0\sin\theta_0$.
Closing speed along $x$: $v_0\cos\theta_0+u\cos\theta_1$, so $T=\dfrac{L}{v_0(\cos\theta_0+\sin\theta_0\cot\theta_1)}=\dfrac{L\sin\theta_1}{v_0\sin(\theta_0+\theta_1)}$.
$T_1=\dfrac{L\sin45^\circ}{v_0}$, $T_2=\dfrac{L\sin30^\circ}{v_0}$ (both with $\sin90^\circ=1$).
$\left(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{1/\sqrt2}{1/2}\right)^2=2$.

questions.text: A charge is kept at the central point P of a cylindrical region. The two edges subtend a half-angle $\theta$ at P, as shown in the figure. When $\theta=30^\circ$, then the electric flux through the curved surface of the cylinder is $\Phi$. If $\theta=60^\circ$, then the electric flux through the curved surface becomes $\Phi/\sqrt n$, where the value of $n$ is______.
questions.sol:
Each flat face subtends a cone of half-angle $\theta$, solid angle $2\pi(1-\cos\theta)$, so it receives a fraction $\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{2}$ of the total flux $\dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}$.
Curved surface: $\dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}\left[1-2\cdot\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{2}\right]=\dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}\cos\theta$.
$\theta=30^\circ$: $\Phi=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}$; $\theta=60^\circ$: $\dfrac12\dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}=\dfrac{\Phi}{\sqrt3}$.
$n=3$.

questions.text: Two equilateral-triangular prisms $\mathrm{P_1}$ and $\mathrm{P_2}$ are kept with their sides parallel to each other, in vacuum, as shown in the figure. A light ray enters prism $\mathrm{P_1}$ at an angle of incidence $\theta$ such that the outgoing ray undergoes minimum deviation in prism $\mathrm{P_2}$. If the respective refractive indices of $\mathrm{P_1}$ and $\mathrm{P_2}$ are $\sqrt{\dfrac32}$ and $\sqrt3$, then $\theta=\sin^{-1}\left[\sqrt{\dfrac32}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{\beta}\right)\right]$, where the value of $\beta$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Minimum deviation in $\mathrm{P_2}$ ($A=60^\circ$): internal angle $30^\circ$, so the incidence on $\mathrm{P_2}$ satisfies $\sin i=\sqrt3\sin30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, $i=60^\circ$.
The facing faces are parallel, so the ray leaves $\mathrm{P_1}$ at $60^\circ$: $\sin r_2=\dfrac{\sin60^\circ}{\sqrt{3/2}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, $r_2=45^\circ$.
$r_1=60^\circ-45^\circ=15^\circ$, so $\sin\theta=\sqrt{\dfrac32}\sin15^\circ=\sqrt{\dfrac32}\sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}$.
$\beta=12$.

questions.text:
An infinitely long thin wire, having a uniform charge density per unit length of $5$ nC/m, is passing through a spherical shell of radius $1$ m, as shown in the figure. A $10$ nC charge is distributed uniformly over the spherical shell. If the configuration of the charges remains static, the magnitude of the potential difference between points P and R, in Volt, is ______.
[Given: In SI units $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}=9\times10^9$, $\ln2=0.7$. Ignore the area pierced by the wire.]
questions.sol:
P is $0.5$ m and R is $2$ m from the wire (and from the centre).
Shell: $V_P=\dfrac{kQ}{1}=90$ V (inside), $V_R=\dfrac{kQ}{2}=45$ V; difference $45$ V.
Wire: $V_P-V_R=2k\lambda\ln\dfrac{2}{0.5}=2(9\times10^9)(5\times10^{-9})(2\ln2)=90\times1.4=126$ V.
Both contributions make P higher: $|V_P-V_R|=126+45=171$ V.

questions.text: A spherical soap bubble inside an air chamber at pressure $P_0=10^5$ Pa has a certain radius so that the excess pressure inside the bubble is $\Delta P=144$ Pa. Now, the chamber pressure is reduced to $8P_0/27$ so that the bubble radius and its excess pressure change. In this process, all the temperatures remain unchanged. Assume air to be an ideal gas and the excess pressure $\Delta P$ in both the cases to be much smaller than the chamber pressure. The new excess pressure $\Delta P$ in Pa is ______.
questions.sol:
Since $\Delta P\ll$ chamber pressure, the gas inside is at about the chamber pressure.
Isothermal: $P_0r_1^3=\dfrac{8P_0}{27}r_2^3\Rightarrow r_2=\dfrac32r_1$.
$\Delta P=\dfrac{4T}{r}$, so $\Delta P_2=144\times\dfrac23=96$ Pa.

questions.text:
In a Young’s double slit experiment, each of the two slits A and B, as shown in the figure, are oscillating about their fixed center and with a mean separation of $0.8$ mm. The distance between the slits at time $t$ is given by $d=(0.8+0.04\sin\omega t)$ mm, where $\omega=0.08\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. The distance of the screen from the slits is $1$ m and the wavelength of the light used to illuminate the slits is $6000$ Å. The interference pattern on the screen changes with time, while the central bright fringe (zeroth fringe) remains fixed at point O.

The $8^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe above the point O oscillates with time between two extreme positions. The separation between these two extreme positions, in micrometer ($\mu$m), is ______.
questions.sol:
$y_8=\dfrac{8\lambda D}{d}=\dfrac{8(6\times10^{-7})(1)}{d}=\dfrac{4.8\times10^{-6}}{d}$ m.
$d$ varies between $0.76$ mm and $0.84$ mm.
$y_{\max}=\dfrac{4.8\times10^{-6}}{0.76\times10^{-3}}=6.3158$ mm, $y_{\min}=\dfrac{4.8\times10^{-6}}{0.84\times10^{-3}}=5.7143$ mm.
Separation $=0.6015$ mm $\approx601.5\ \mu$m (within $598$ to $602$).

questions.text:
In a Young’s double slit experiment, each of the two slits A and B, as shown in the figure, are oscillating about their fixed center and with a mean separation of $0.8$ mm. The distance between the slits at time $t$ is given by $d=(0.8+0.04\sin\omega t)$ mm, where $\omega=0.08\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. The distance of the screen from the slits is $1$ m and the wavelength of the light used to illuminate the slits is $6000$ Å. The interference pattern on the screen changes with time, while the central bright fringe (zeroth fringe) remains fixed at point O.

The maximum speed in $\mu$m/s at which the $8^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe will move is __________.
questions.sol:
$y_8=\dfrac{8\lambda D}{d}$, so $\left|\dfrac{dy_8}{dt}\right|=\dfrac{8\lambda D}{d^2}\left|\dfrac{dd}{dt}\right|$, with $\dfrac{dd}{dt}=0.04\omega\cos\omega t$ mm/s.
The speed is greatest near $\cos\omega t=\pm1$, where $d=0.8$ mm and $\left|\dfrac{dd}{dt}\right|=0.04\times0.08=3.2\times10^{-3}$ mm/s $=3.2\times10^{-6}$ m/s.
$v_{\max}\approx\dfrac{4.8\times10^{-6}\times3.2\times10^{-6}}{(0.8\times10^{-3})^2}=2.4\times10^{-5}$ m/s $=24\ \mu$m/s (the small variation of $d$ shifts this only to about $24.1$).

questions.text:
Two particles, 1 and 2, each of mass $m$, are connected by a massless spring, and are on a horizontal frictionless plane, as shown in the figure. Initially, the two particles, with their center of mass at $x_0$, are oscillating with amplitude $a$ and angular frequency $\omega$. Thus, their positions at time $t$ are given by $x_1(t)=(x_0+d)+a\sin\omega t$ and $x_2(t)=(x_0-d)-a\sin\omega t$, respectively, where $d>2a$. Particle 3 of mass $m$ moves towards this system with speed $u_0=a\omega/2$, and undergoes instantaneous elastic collision with particle 2, at time $t_0$. Finally, particles 1 and 2 acquire a center of mass speed $v_{\text{cm}}$ and oscillate with amplitude $b$ and the same angular frequency $\omega$.

If the collision occurs at time $t_0=0$, the value of $v_{\text{cm}}/(a\omega)$ will be __________.
questions.sol:
At $t=0$: $\dot x_1=a\omega$, $\dot x_2=-a\omega$ (particle 2 moving towards particle 3).
Elastic collision of equal masses exchanges velocities: particle 2 gets $+\dfrac{a\omega}{2}$.
$v_{\text{cm}}=\dfrac{a\omega+a\omega/2}{2}=\dfrac34a\omega$.
$v_{\text{cm}}/(a\omega)=0.75$.

questions.text:
Two particles, 1 and 2, each of mass $m$, are connected by a massless spring, and are on a horizontal frictionless plane, as shown in the figure. Initially, the two particles, with their center of mass at $x_0$, are oscillating with amplitude $a$ and angular frequency $\omega$. Thus, their positions at time $t$ are given by $x_1(t)=(x_0+d)+a\sin\omega t$ and $x_2(t)=(x_0-d)-a\sin\omega t$, respectively, where $d>2a$. Particle 3 of mass $m$ moves towards this system with speed $u_0=a\omega/2$, and undergoes instantaneous elastic collision with particle 2, at time $t_0$. Finally, particles 1 and 2 acquire a center of mass speed $v_{\text{cm}}$ and oscillate with amplitude $b$ and the same angular frequency $\omega$.

If the collision occurs at time $t_0=\pi/(2\omega)$, then the value of $4b^2/a^2$ will be ________.
questions.sol:
At $t_0=\dfrac{\pi}{2\omega}$ both particles are momentarily at rest, each displaced by $a$ from its equilibrium relative to the CM (spring at maximum stretch).
After the collision particle 2 has $\dfrac{a\omega}{2}$ and particle 1 has $0$, so $v_{\text{cm}}=\dfrac{a\omega}{4}$; relative to the CM each particle moves at $\dfrac{a\omega}{4}$ while displaced by $a$.
$b^2=a^2+\left(\dfrac{a\omega/4}{\omega}\right)^2=\dfrac{17}{16}a^2$.
$\dfrac{4b^2}{a^2}=\dfrac{17}{4}=4.25$.

questions.text: In a metal deficient oxide sample, $\mathbf{M_XY_2O_4}$ ($\mathbf{M}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ are metals), $\mathbf{M}$ is present in both +2 and +3 oxidation states and $\mathbf{Y}$ is in +3 oxidation state. If the fraction of $\mathbf{M^{2+}}$ ions present in $\mathbf{M}$ is $\dfrac13$, the value of $\mathbf{X}$ is _____.
questions.sol:
Charge balance: $2(+3)+X\cdot(\text{average charge of M})=8$, so $X\times(\text{average charge})=2$.
Average charge of M $=\dfrac13(2)+\dfrac23(3)=\dfrac83$.
$X=\dfrac{2}{8/3}=0.75$ → (D).

questions.text: The species formed on fluorination of phosphorus pentachloride in a polar organic solvent are
questions.note: Official final key: A or B (either option is awarded marks).

In a polar solvent $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ ionises as $\mathrm{[PCl_4]^+[PCl_6]^-}$, so its fluorination gives ionic chloro/fluoro-phosphonium salts, not neutral molecules.

(C) and (D) involve reduction to P(III) or neutral $\mathrm{PF_5}$, which a simple halide exchange does not give.

questions.text:
An aqueous solution of hydrazine ($\mathrm{N_2H_4}$) is electrochemically oxidized by $\mathrm{O_2}$, thereby releasing chemical energy in the form of electrical energy. One of the products generated from the electrochemical reaction is $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$.
Choose the correct statement(s) about the above process
options: $\mathrm{OH^-}$ ions react with $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$ at the anode to form $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$ and water, releasing 4 electrons to the anode.
At the cathode, $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$ breaks to $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$ and nascent hydrogen released at the electrode reacts with oxygen to form water.
At the cathode, molecular oxygen gets converted to $\mathrm{OH^-}$.
Oxides of nitrogen are major by-products of the electrochemical process.
questions.sol:
Hydrazine fuel cell (alkaline):
Anode: $\mathrm{N_2H_4+4OH^-\to N_2+4H_2O+4e^-}$ → (A) true.
Cathode: $\mathrm{O_2+2H_2O+4e^-\to4OH^-}$ → (C) true; hydrazine is not oxidised at the cathode → (B) false.
Overall: $\mathrm{N_2H_4+O_2\to N_2+2H_2O}$; no oxides of nitrogen → (D) false.
Answer: (A), (C).

questions.text: The option(s) with correct sequence of reagents for the conversion of $\mathbf{P}$ to $\mathbf{Q}$ is(are)
options: i) Lindlar’s catalyst, $\mathrm{H_2}$; ii) $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$; iii) $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$; iv) $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$
i) Lindlar’s catalyst, $\mathrm{H_2}$; ii) $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$; iii) $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$; iv) $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$
i) $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$; ii) $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$; iii) $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$; iv) Lindlar’s catalyst, $\mathrm{H_2}$
i) Lindlar’s catalyst, $\mathrm{H_2}$; ii) $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$; iii) $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$; iv) $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$
questions.sol:
Changes needed: two $\mathrm{C\equiv C}\to$ cis $\mathrm{C=C}$ (Lindlar, $\mathrm{H_2}$); ring $\mathrm{C=O}\to$ CH–OH ($\mathrm{NaBH_4}$, which leaves ester and nitrile alone); $\mathrm{-CN}\to\mathrm{-CHO}$ (Stephen: $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$ then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$); acetate and ethyl ester $\to$ OH and $\mathrm{CO_2H}$ ($\mathrm{H_3O^+}$).
$\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ must act before any CHO (or the Stephen imine) is present, otherwise it reduces that too.
(A): $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ after $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}$ reduces the aldimine → wrong. (B): $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ last reduces the CHO → wrong.
(C) and (D) reduce the ketone first, then do the Stephen reduction and hydrolysis; Lindlar can be first or last → correct.
Answer: (C), (D).

questions.text:
To form a complete monolayer of acetic acid on 1g of charcoal, 100 mL of 0.5 M acetic acid was used. Some of the acetic acid remained unadsorbed. To neutralize the unadsorbed acetic acid, 40 mL of 1 M NaOH solution was required. If each molecule of acetic acid occupies $\mathbf{P}$ $\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ surface area on charcoal, the value of $\mathbf{P}$ is _____.
[Use given data: Surface area of charcoal $=1.5\times10^2\ \mathrm{m^2g^{-1}}$; Avogadro’s number $(N_A)=6.0\times10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}$]
questions.sol:
Acetic acid taken $=0.1\times0.5=0.05$ mol; unadsorbed $=0.04\times1=0.04$ mol; adsorbed $=0.01$ mol.
Molecules adsorbed $=0.01\times6.0\times10^{23}=6.0\times10^{21}$.
Area per molecule $=\dfrac{150}{6.0\times10^{21}}=2.5\times10^{-20}=2500\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.
$\mathbf{P}$ $=2500$.

Vessel-1 contains $w_2$ g of a non-volatile solute $\mathbf{X}$ dissolved in $w_1$ g of water. Vessel-2 contains $w_2$ g of another non-volatile solute $\mathbf{Y}$ dissolved in $w_1$ g of water. Both the vessels are at the same temperature and pressure. The molar mass of $\mathbf{X}$ is 80% of that of $\mathbf{Y}$. The van’t Hoff factor for $\mathbf{X}$ is 1.2 times of that of $\mathbf{Y}$ for their respective concentrations.
The elevation of boiling point for solution in Vessel-1 is _____ % of the solution in Vessel-2.
questions.sol:
$\Delta T_b=iK_b\dfrac{w_2\times1000}{M\,w_1}$, so with equal $w_1$, $w_2$: $\dfrac{\Delta T_{b,1}}{\Delta T_{b,2}}=\dfrac{i_X}{i_Y}\cdot\dfrac{M_Y}{M_X}$.
$=1.2\times\dfrac{1}{0.8}=1.5$.
So it is $150\%$.

questions.text:
For a double strand DNA, one strand is given below:
5′ – A G T C A C G T A A G T C – 3′
The amount of energy required to split the double strand DNA into two single strands is _____ kcal $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$.
[Given: Average energy per H-bond for A-T base pair $=1.0$ kcal $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, G-C base pair $=1.5$ kcal $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, and A-U base pair $=1.25$ kcal $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. Ignore electrostatic repulsion between the phosphate groups.]
questions.sol:
Bases: A = 4, T = 3, G = 3, C = 3, so the duplex has $7$ A-T pairs and $6$ G-C pairs.
A-T has 2 H-bonds, G-C has 3 H-bonds (A-U is not present in DNA).
Energy $=7\times2\times1.0+6\times3\times1.5=14+27=41$ kcal $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text:
A sample initially contains only U-238 isotope of uranium. With time, some of the U-238 radioactively decays into Pb-206 while the rest of it remains undisintegrated.
When the age of the sample is $\mathbf{P}$ $\times10^8$ years, the ratio of mass of Pb-206 to that of U-238 in the sample is found to be 7. The value of $\mathbf{P}$ is _____.
[Given: Half-life of U-238 is $4.5\times10^9$ years; $\log_e2=0.693$]
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone.
questions.sol:
Mole ratio $\dfrac{N_{\mathrm{Pb}}}{N_{\mathrm U}}=7\times\dfrac{238}{206}=8.087$, so $\dfrac{N_0}{N}=9.087$.
$t=\dfrac{t_{1/2}}{0.693}\ln\dfrac{N_0}{N}=\dfrac{4.5\times10^9}{0.693}\times2.207\approx1.43\times10^{10}$ years, i.e. $\mathbf{P}$ $\approx143$ (not an integer).
If the mass ratio were taken as the atom ratio, $\dfrac{N_0}{N}=8$ (three half-lives) and $\mathbf{P}$ $=135$; the question is ambiguous.
The official final key dropped this question (marks to all).

questions.text: Among $\mathrm{[Co(CN)_4]^{4-}}$, $\mathrm{[Co(CO)_3(NO)]}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{[PCl_4]^+}$, $\mathrm{[PdCl_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{[ICl_4]^-}$, $\mathrm{[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{P_4}$ the total number of species with tetrahedral geometry is _____.

questions.text:
An organic compound $\mathbf{P}$ having molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_6O_3}$ gives ferric chloride test and does not have intramolecular hydrogen bond. The compound $\mathbf{P}$ reacts with 3 equivalents of $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$ to produce oxime $\mathbf{Q}$. Treatment of $\mathbf{P}$ with excess methyl iodide in the presence of KOH produces compound $\mathbf{R}$ as the major product. Reaction of $\mathbf{R}$ with excess iso-butylmagnesium bromide followed by treatment with $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ gives compound $\mathbf{S}$ as the major product.
The total number of methyl $(-\mathrm{CH_3})$ group(s) in compound $\mathbf{S}$ is _____.
questions.note: Official final key: 6 or 12 (either value is awarded marks).
questions.sol:
$\mathbf{P}$ is phloroglucinol (1,3,5-trihydroxybenzene): phenolic ($\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ test), OH groups meta so no intramolecular H-bond, and its keto form (cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione) gives a trioxime $\mathbf{Q}$.
Excess $\mathrm{CH_3I}$/KOH C-methylates all three $\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups of the trione: $\mathbf{R}$ = 2,2,4,4,6,6-hexamethylcyclohexane-1,3,5-trione (6 $\mathrm{CH_3}$).
The carbonyls are very hindered, so the bulky iso-butyl Grignard acts as a reducing agent ($\beta$-hydride transfer): $\mathbf{S}$ = 2,2,4,4,6,6-hexamethylcyclohexane-1,3,5-triol, with $6$ $\mathrm{CH_3}$ groups.
If instead the Grignard adds, each iso-butyl brings 2 more $\mathrm{CH_3}$, giving $6+6=12$.
Answer: $6$ (the official key also accepts $12$).

questions.stem: Paragraph I for Question Nos. 14 and 15
questions.text:
An organic compound $\mathbf{P}$ with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{18}O_2}$ decolorizes bromine water and also shows positive iodoform test. $\mathbf{P}$ on ozonolysis followed by treatment with $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ gives $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$. While compound $\mathbf{Q}$ shows positive iodoform test, compound $\mathbf{R}$ does not give positive iodoform test. $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ on oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) followed by heating give $\mathbf{S}$ and $\mathbf{T}$, respectively. Both $\mathbf{S}$ and $\mathbf{T}$ show positive iodoform test.
Complete copolymerization of 500 moles of $\mathbf{Q}$ and 500 moles of $\mathbf{R}$ gives one mole of a single acyclic copolymer $\mathbf{U}$.
[Given, atomic mass: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]

Sum of number of oxygen atoms in $\mathbf{S}$ and $\mathbf{T}$ is _____.
questions.note: Official final key: 2 or 4 (either value is awarded marks).
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_9H_{18}O_2}$ has one C=C; ozonolysis with $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ gives two acids, and since $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ copolymerise (polyester) both are hydroxy acids.
$\mathbf{P}$ $=\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH{=}CHCH_2CH(OH)CH_2CH_3}$ (iodoform +).
$\mathbf{Q}$ $=\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_2COOH}$ (iodoform +); $\mathbf{R}$ $=\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(OH)CH_2COOH}$ (iodoform −).
PCC gives the $\beta$-keto acids, which lose $\mathrm{CO_2}$ on heating: $\mathbf{S}$ = acetone, $\mathbf{T}$ = butan-2-one (both iodoform +).
Oxygen atoms: $1+1=2$ (the official key also accepts $4$).

Complete copolymerization of 500 moles of $\mathbf{Q}$ and 500 moles of $\mathbf{R}$ gives one mole of a single acyclic copolymer $\mathbf{U}$.

The molecular weight of $\mathbf{U}$ is _____.
questions.sol:
$\mathbf{Q}$ $=\mathrm{C_4H_8O_3}$ ($M=104$), $\mathbf{R}$ $=\mathrm{C_5H_{10}O_3}$ ($M=118$).
A single acyclic chain of $1000$ hydroxy-acid units has $999$ ester links, each releasing one $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
$M(\mathbf U)=500(104)+500(118)-999(18)=111000-17982=93018$.

questions.stem: Paragraph II for Question Nos. 16 and 17
questions.text:
When potassium iodide is added to an aqueous solution of potassium ferricyanide, a reversible reaction is observed in which a complex $\mathbf{P}$ is formed. In a strong acidic medium, the equilibrium shifts completely towards $\mathbf{P}$. Addition of zinc chloride to $\mathbf{P}$ in a slightly acidic medium results in a sparingly soluble complex $\mathbf{Q}$.

The number of moles of potassium iodide required to produce two moles of $\mathbf{P}$ is _____.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2K_3[Fe(CN)_6]+2KI\rightleftharpoons 2K_4[Fe(CN)_6]+I_2}$; in strong acid the equilibrium shifts fully to the right.
$\mathbf{P}$ $=\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$; one KI is needed per $\mathbf{P}$.
For two moles of $\mathbf{P}$: $2$ moles of KI.

questions.stem: Paragraph II for Question Nos. 16 and 17
questions.text:
When potassium iodide is added to an aqueous solution of potassium ferricyanide, a reversible reaction is observed in which a complex $\mathbf{P}$ is formed. In a strong acidic medium, the equilibrium shifts completely towards $\mathbf{P}$. Addition of zinc chloride to $\mathbf{P}$ in a slightly acidic medium results in a sparingly soluble complex $\mathbf{Q}$.

The number of zinc ions present in the molecular formula of $\mathbf{Q}$ is _____.
questions.note: Official final key: 2 or 3 (either value is awarded marks).
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ precipitates ferrocyanide: $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]+2ZnCl_2\to Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]\downarrow+4KCl}$, so $\mathbf{Q}$ $=\mathrm{Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$ with $2$ zinc ions.
With excess ferrocyanide the double salt $\mathrm{K_2Zn_3[Fe(CN)_6]_2}$ (3 zinc ions) forms instead.
Answer: $2$ (the official key also accepts $3$).
